business-api-context · Bunkai TMS

Business API map

Built 2026-10-12 from upex-bunkai-tms origin/staging 98ee1b4 (2026-10-11): route handlers, lib/api/, the generated contract public/openapi.json (identical to what the openapi MCP serves) and the data and E2E maps of the same date. No live API call was made: every status code here is read from code. Every fact a figure shows is also in the text.

Overview

What the API lets the business do. Bunkai's API is the same surface the web app uses, so anything a QA team does in the browser can also be done by a script, a CI pipeline or an AI agent: sign in, build a project's module tree and user stories (or pull them from Jira), author ATCs (Acceptance Test Cases) anchored to acceptance criteria, chain them into Tests, start and record Runs, file and triage bugs, and read coverage, traceability and run reports. A test team can therefore run its whole loop headlessly and still produce the same evidence trail a person would.

Who may do what is decided in two places. The API gateway decides how a caller may arrive (public, browser session only, any signed-in caller, or a token carrying the right scope); the database decides what that person may touch (their workspace role: viewer, member, admin, owner, enforced by Row Level Security and the business functions). A token never has more power than the person who issued it; it can only have less. A handful of owner actions (delete or restore a workspace, export its data, issue or revoke tokens) are deliberately reserved for a person in a browser.

Money and irreversible actions sit behind the owner: the Cloud upgrade goes through Stripe and only takes effect when Stripe confirms payment, and deleting a workspace ends access for everyone immediately with a 30-day window to restore. Three things run without a person: a daily email digest triggered by Vercel Cron, the Stripe webhook, and background workers that do Jira imports, data exports and deletion emails after the request has answered.

Permission and auth model

Every handler under app/api/ is wrapped by withApiHandler (lib/api/handler.ts) and must declare one of four postures; there is no default, so a route without one does not compile. A source scan (lib/api/route-posture-scan.ts) diffs every handler against the committed snapshot lib/api/route-capability-coverage.snapshot.json. Re-run against the snapshot commit: 107 handlers (105 under app/api/, 2 under app/auth/), identical to the snapshot. The middleware (middleware.ts) only refreshes the session cookie on /api/*; it never blocks an API request.

Schemes

Four credential schemes coexist, each with its own section: the browser cookie session (auth-cookie-session), the personal access token (auth-pat), and two system secrets (auth-system-callers). The OpenAPI contract declares them as cookieAuth (cookie sb-{project-ref}-auth-token), bearerAuth and cronAuth; the Stripe signature is not in the contract.

Precedence and refusals

  • A request carrying Authorization: Bearer … is always treated as a PAT, even when a session cookie is also present (bearer first, resolveIdentity).
  • No credential on a non-public route: 401 unauthorized "Authentication required."
  • Any PAT failure (wrong shape, unknown prefix, hash mismatch, revoked, expired): one uniform 401 unauthorized "Invalid token." The caller cannot tell which check failed.
  • Missing scope: 403 forbidden with details.reason = missing_capability and details.required_capability, so a client can tell it from a role refusal, which is also 403.
  • A PAT on a cookie-only route: 403 forbidden with the route's reason (for example "Personal access tokens cannot issue tokens. Use a browser session.").
  • Role refusals come from Postgres: a write by a viewer surfaces as 403 forbidden (details.reason = not_a_member); a resource in a workspace the caller cannot see answers 404, the same as a missing one.

Scheme: browser cookie session

The browser scheme. A person proves who they are to Supabase Auth and receives the Supabase session cookie (sb-*); the API reads it on every call.

  1. Magic link: POST /api/v1/auth/magic-link asks Supabase Auth to email a link (only to an existing account; shouldCreateUser is false). The answer is always { ok: true }, also for an unknown address (anti-enumeration); a Supabase rate limit surfaces as 429 rate_limited. An audit row is written best-effort.
  2. The emailed link lands on GET /auth/callback, which verifies the token hash statelessly (so a link requested on a laptop works on a phone) and sets the session cookie, then redirects to next (root-relative only, default /projects). Failures redirect to /login?error=magic_link_invalid.
  3. OAuth (GitHub, Google): GET /auth/oauth/{provider} sets a state cookie and redirects to the provider; the callback rejects a state mismatch with 403 OAUTH_STATE_MISMATCH before exchanging the code.
  4. Headless password sign-in and email-code confirmation (auth-pat) also set the cookie on the response, so a script can hold a browser-grade session.
  5. Every later /api/v1 call: the gateway calls Supabase getUser; the principal holds all four scopes and the handler queries Postgres with the user's own session, so RLS filters the rows.
  6. Refresh: the middleware calls getUser on every matched request and writes refreshed cookies back; there is no separate refresh endpoint.
  7. The active workspace is a separate preference cookie (bk_active_ws) set by POST /api/v1/me/active-workspace (cookie-only, 403 "You are not a member of that workspace." for a foreign id).

Scheme: personal access token (PAT)

The programmatic scheme for CLIs, CI and AI agents. A PAT acts as the person who issued it, narrowed by its scopes; the token string is bk_pat_{12-char prefix}.{secret} and is shown exactly once.

How to obtain one

PathCredential neededScopesWorkspace bindingExpiry
POST /api/v1/auth/signin (email + password)none (public)default atc:read, atc:write, run:execute; workspace:admin refused (403)none (global token)never, unless pat_expires_in_days (1 to 365)
POST /api/v1/auth/signup then POST /api/v1/auth/confirm (6 to 8 digit email code)none (public)same as sign-innonesame as sign-in
POST /api/v1/tokensbrowser session onlyany non-empty subset of the fouroptional workspace_id; mandatory for workspace:admin, which also needs admin or owner role therenever, unless expires_in_days (1 to 365)

Sign-up answers 202 pending_confirmation and issues nothing; the token and session come only from /auth/confirm. Sign-in and confirm return the Supabase session tokens next to the PAT, but those session tokens are not accepted as a bearer on /api/v1: the bearer branch only accepts the bk_pat_ family and answers 401 otherwise.

On every call

  1. The gateway reads the bearer, looks the token up by prefix with the service-role client and compares the SHA-256 of the secret against the separate secret table.
  2. A revoked or expired token gets the same 401 as a forged one. last_used_at is updated fire-and-forget.
  3. The route scope is checked (403 missing_capability); for the 7 workspace:admin handlers the token must also be bound to the target workspace (403 "This token is not scoped to a workspace…" or "…scoped to a different workspace.").
  4. The API mints a 60-second user JWT (signed with the Supabase JWT secret, never returned) so Postgres RLS sees the token owner exactly as for a browser call. Scopes are not in that JWT: Postgres enforces the role, the API enforces the scope.

End of life

Revocation (DELETE /api/v1/tokens/{id}, browser only) stamps revoked_at; rows are never deleted. Leaving a workspace or deleting it revokes the tokens bound to it, and a pipeline using one starts getting 401. A PAT can never issue or revoke a PAT. GET /api/v1/tokens (any credential) lists the caller's own tokens without secrets.

Scheme: system callers (cron secret, Stripe signature)

Two callers are not people and hold no PAT. Both routes declare the public posture and authenticate inside the handler.

CallerRouteCredentialRefusalWhat it changes
Vercel Cron, daily 08:00 UTC (registered from the production deployment only, vercel.json)GET /api/v1/admin/send-digest (cron); POST is the manual retryAuthorization: Bearer {CRON_SECRET} (cronAuth in the contract)401 unauthorized "Invalid or missing CRON_SECRET."claims one digest row per user and UTC day, sends one Resend email per user, returns a run summary
StripePOST /api/v1/billing/webhook (not in the OpenAPI contract)stripe-signature header verified against the webhook secret400 bad_request when missing or invalidapplies checkout events to the checkout session and, when paid, upgrades the workspace plan

Webhook outcomes: an event type outside the four checkout events answers 200 ignored; a checkout session the database does not know yet answers 502 upstream_error so Stripe redelivers; a database failure answers 500. Duplicate events are deduplicated by event id inside bunkai_apply_billing_checkout_webhook_event.

Scope design worth knowing: there is no bug scope and no report scope. Filing, assigning and advancing bugs need atc:write; every report and list needs atc:read; only the four run-state writes need run:execute. A token with run:execute alone can start and close Runs but cannot read the Test it runs (GET /tests/{id} needs atc:read).

Group: sign-up and sign-in

Who calls it: the login page (email-first form) and headless clients. Why: get an account and a credential. What it changes: Supabase Auth users and sessions; a PAT row on confirm and sign-in; a magic-link audit row.

OperationBusiness meaningNotable answers
POST /auth/check-emailRoute an entered email to password, code entry or sign-up200 { exists, confirmed }: deliberately reveals whether an account exists
POST /auth/signupCreate an unconfirmed account and email a code202 pending_confirmation; 409 existing account; 429 Supabase rate limit
POST /auth/confirmProve the email with the code; get session + PAT200; 401 invalid or expired code; 403 if workspace:admin requested
POST /auth/resendSend the code again202 sent; 429
POST /auth/signinPassword sign-in; get session + PAT200; 401 "Invalid email or password." (uniform)
POST /auth/magic-linkEmail a sign-in link to an existing accountalways 200 { ok: true } except 429 and 502

Passwords are 8 to 128 characters at sign-up and 6 to 128 at sign-in. Data: flow-sign-in-and-onboarding. Features: feature-access (FEAT-001, FEAT-002). Journey: journey-sign-in-and-onboarding.

Group: identity and tokens

Who calls it: the app shell (who am I, which workspace is active), Settings, Tokens, and automation clients checking who they are. What it changes: the active-workspace cookie and access_tokens.

  • GET /me (any credential): the principal, how it authenticated, its workspaces and an effective workspace (the token's binding, else the first visible one).
  • POST /me/active-workspace (cookie only): set the browser's active workspace; a PAT passes workspace_id on each request instead (for example POST /tests answers 422 "workspace_id is required for token-authenticated calls.").
  • GET /tokens (any credential), POST /tokens and DELETE /tokens/{id} (cookie only): list, issue (201, secret shown once) and revoke PATs. Details in auth-pat.

Data: entity-access-token, state-access-token. Features: FEAT-003 (feature-access), FEAT-005 (feature-workspace).

Group: workspace lifecycle

The tenant itself: create it, rename it, leave it, take the data out, delete it and bring it back. Highest blast radius in the API: one call can end access for a whole team.

Group: team invites

Who calls it: an admin or owner growing the team, and the invitee redeeming the link. Bunkai sends no invite email: the issue call returns the accept URL once and the inviter shares it.

  • Issue, list, rotate, revoke (POST|GET /workspaces/{id}/invites, POST|DELETE …/invites/{inviteId}): workspace:admin, token bound to that workspace, admin or owner (RLS). Roles offered: viewer, member, admin; never owner. Inviting an existing active member is refused.
  • Accept (POST /invites/accept): any authenticated caller, because the invitee is not a member yet. Full answer table in journey-invite-and-join.
  • Seats are not checked when inviting or accepting (data map flow-invite-and-membership).

Data: entity-invite, state-invite. Features: FEAT-006 (feature-workspace).

Group: billing and plan

The only place money changes hands. Who calls it: the billing settings pages, and Stripe.

  • GET /workspaces/{id}/billing (atc:read): plan, purchased and active seats, project count, oldest run age; admins and owners only, others get 404.
  • POST /workspaces/{id}/billing/checkout (workspace:admin, bound token, Idempotency-Key required, owner only): returns the Stripe hosted checkout URL. 422 plan_not_upgradable on Cloud or Enterprise, 422 seat_quantity_invalid, 409 checkout_in_progress, 503 payment_processor_unavailable.
  • POST …/billing/checkout/cancel (same gate): expire the open session after Stripe's cancel page.
  • Stripe webhook: see auth-system-callers. Plan limits: only the project limit is enforced (422 project_limit_reached on project creation).

Data: flow-billing-upgrade, state-checkout-session, integration-stripe. Features: FEAT-007 (feature-workspace).

Group: project structure

Describes the product under test: projects, a module tree, user stories and their ordered acceptance criteria. Who calls it: members in the project explorer and automation that seeds structure. What it changes: projects, modules, user_stories, acceptance_criteria.

  • Every DELETE here archives (soft delete), never removes rows: module subtree, user story, criterion. Archiving the last active criterion drops the story back to draft.
  • Story status ready_to_test requires at least one active criterion.
  • Module rename and move are validated by the database (sibling slug clash, cycles, depth above 6).
  • There is no project list or project read endpoint in the contract: projects are listed through GET /workspaces/{id}/recent-projects (group-insights).

Data: entity-module, entity-user-story, state-user-story, flow-author-structure. Features: FEAT-010, FEAT-011, FEAT-012 (feature-authoring).

Group: Jira import

Pulls user stories and criteria from Jira by JQL, one way. POST /imports (atc:write, member) answers 202 with a job id; GET /imports/{id} (atc:read) is polled until completed or failed. One active import per project (409). Traced in journey-jira-import.

Data: flow-jira-import, state-async-job, integration-jira. Features: FEAT-013 (feature-authoring).

Group: ATC authoring and library

The core asset of the product. Writes (atc:write, member): create (201), edit with the expected version (full replace of steps, assertions and criteria bindings), duplicate. Reads (atc:read): which Tests use an ATC, full-text search by title and tags, whole-library CSV export.

  • Anchoring is enforced on every write: criteria must belong to the story (422 ac_outside_user_story), the module must be in the story's project subtree (422 module_outside_project_subtree).
  • Optimistic lock: a stale version answers 409 conflict with details.reason = version_conflict and details.current_version. An edit reports how many Tests are affected, because Tests hold references, not copies.
  • At most 10 tags; title at least 3 characters; slug collision 409 slug_collision (retryable).
  • There is no ATC delete endpoint and no single-ATC read in the contract.

Data: entity-atc, flow-author-atc. Features: FEAT-014, FEAT-015 (feature-authoring). Journey: journey-author-atc.

Group: test design

Turns ATCs into executable scenarios and plans: Tests (ordered chains of ATC references), test plans, milestones and the environments a Run must name.

AreaWrites (atc:write)Rules a client hits
Testscreate (Idempotency-Key required, PAT must pass workspace_id), reorder, replace tags422 chain_empty; 404 when a chained ATC is outside the workspace; reorder must keep the same ATCs (422 chain_mismatch / chain_invalid) and the current version (409)
Test planscreate, edit, add Tests (Idempotency-Key required), remove a Testa Test whose chain leaves the plan's project: 422 test_outside_plan_project; closed plan: 409; nothing closes a plan
Milestonescreate, editname unique per project; date within 5 years
Environmentscreate, rename, deletedelete refused with 409 while Runs reference it; a new project has none, so no Run can start

Data: entity-test, flow-compose-test-and-plan, flow-environments, state-test-plan. Features: FEAT-016 to FEAT-019 (feature-test-design).

Group: run execution

Records what was executed, where, by whom and with what result. The four state-changing calls are the only ones that need run:execute: start (POST /runs), mark a step, finish with a verdict, abort with a reason. Reads (atc:read): one Run with its frozen chain, a project run report, a Test's run history, the workspace's active runs.

  • Executor: a browser start is always recorded as human; a PAT may declare human, agent or ci (422 otherwise).
  • Two duplicate guards: the Idempotency-Key header (required, replays the stored answer) and the start_token body field (same Test and token within 24 hours returns the running Run with 200 instead of 201).
  • Only a running Run accepts marks, finish or abort (409 with reasons run_step_marking_closed, run_not_finishable, run_not_abortable). The finish verdict is the caller's choice, not computed.
  • A Run left without activity for 4 hours is aborted by the database sweep; a later mark gets 409.

Data: entity-run, flow-execute-run, state-run, state-run-step. Features: FEAT-020, FEAT-021 (feature-execution). Journey: journey-execute-run.

Group: defects

Native defect tracking tied to the run step that exposed it. Writes (atc:write, member): file (201), assign or unassign, advance status one stage. Reads (atc:read): filtered list with aggregates, project list, single bug with origin, per-module heatmap, workspace open-bug counts.

  • Filing from a failed step sends only run_step_id; the server derives project, module, run and ATC. Provenance from another project or run is 422.
  • Status is open → in_progress → resolved → closed, one stage at a time, never backward (422 with the next allowed stage in the message).
  • Assignee must be an active, non-viewer member (422). A non-member reading a bug gets 404, a viewer writing gets 403.
  • Bugs have no delete endpoint.

Data: entity-bug, state-bug, flow-file-and-triage-bug. Features: FEAT-022, FEAT-023 (feature-defects). Journey: journey-file-and-triage-bug.

Group: reports and search

What a lead decides on. All read-only, all atc:read, readable by viewers: project and workspace coverage (per criterion: uncovered, not run, executed), one story's full traceability chain (criterion → ATC → Test → Run → Bug), recovery cycles per story, the workspace activity feed (a curated projection, never the raw audit payload), cross-entity search (ATC, Test, Project, Module, Bug, Run) and recent projects for Home. A project the caller cannot see answers 404.

Data: flow-reports, entity-activity-log. Features: FEAT-024 to FEAT-028 (feature-insights). Journey: journey-review-quality (e2e map).

Group: notifications

The personal inbox and email preferences. All five operations are authenticated with no scope, because each caller only ever reads or marks their own rows: the workspace inbox (last 90 days), mark one or all read, read and update one preference cell. Notifications are not created through the API: database triggers write them when a Run closes or a bug is assigned or moves (see journey-execute-run, journey-file-and-triage-bug).

Data: entity-notification, flow-notifications. Features: FEAT-029, FEAT-030 (feature-notifications).

Group: platform and system

  • GET /api/v1: version discovery; OPTIONS /api/v1 answers CORS preflight (not in the contract).
  • GET /api/v1/health: liveness only; it does not touch the database, so a green health check says nothing about Postgres.
  • GET /api/openapi: the contract file, rendered for people at /api/docs (bypass posture).
  • GET|POST /api/v1/admin/send-digest: the daily digest, cron secret only (auth-system-callers).

Features: FEAT-030, FEAT-031 (feature-notifications, feature-public-pages).

Journey: build structure and author an anchored ATC

Purpose: turn a requirement into a reusable, traceable check. This is the value proposition: an ATC that escapes its story and criteria breaks every coverage and traceability report.

  1. Create a project in the workspace (atc:write); the plan's project limit may refuse it (422 project_limit_reached).
  2. Create a module, then a user story under it, then its criteria: the requirement must exist before anything can prove it.
  3. Create the ATC with steps, assertions, the story and at least one of its criteria. The create RPC checks write role, criterion ownership and module subtree in one transaction and audits atc.created.
  4. Edit later with the version read: the database locks the row, compares versions and either replaces content and bumps the version (200, with the count of affected Tests) or answers 409.

Endpoints involved: POST /workspaces/{id}/projects, POST /projects/{id}/modules, POST /modules/{id}/user-stories, POST /user-stories/{id}/acceptance-criteria, POST /atcs, PATCH /atcs/{id}.

Entities touched (business-data-context): entity-module, entity-user-story, entity-atc, flow-author-structure, flow-author-atc.

Features (business-e2e-context): feature-authoring (FEAT-010 to FEAT-014), journey-build-project-structure, journey-author-atc.

Journey: execute a Test as a Run

Purpose: produce immutable execution evidence. A wrong verdict or a lost result defeats the product; this is also the path agents and CI use most.

  1. Compose a Test from ATCs (POST /tests, atc:write, Idempotency-Key required; a PAT names the workspace). Non-empty chain, same-workspace ATCs.
  2. Start a Run (POST /runs, run:execute) with the Test, an environment of the Test's project and optionally a start token and executor mode. The RPC copies the chain into a frozen snapshot with every step pending: later ATC edits never change this Run.
  3. Mark steps passed, failed or blocked with an optional note and evidence URL. Each mark recomputes the run ATC verdict and is pushed live to browsers watching the Run.
  4. Finish with the verdict the executor chooses, or abort with a 3 to 500 character reason. Pending steps become skipped; the starter is notified unless they closed it themselves in a browser.

Endpoints involved: POST /tests, POST /runs, POST /runs/{id}/steps/{stepId}/mark, POST /runs/{id}/finish, POST /runs/{id}/abort, GET /runs/{id}.

Entities touched (business-data-context): entity-test, entity-run, flow-execute-run, state-run, state-run-step, flow-notifications.

Features (business-e2e-context): feature-test-design (FEAT-016, FEAT-017), feature-execution (FEAT-020), journey-compose-test, journey-execute-test-run, journey-automate-via-api.

Journey: file and triage a bug

Purpose: turn a failed step into a tracked defect that keeps its origin, then move it to closure with the right people informed.

  1. File the bug (POST /bugs, atc:write) with the failed run step, title (5 to 200 characters), severity P1 to P4 and up to 10 evidence links. Status starts open; bug.filed is audited.
  2. Assign it to an active non-viewer member; the new assignee is notified (the previous one is not).
  3. Advance the status one stage at a time; the reporter and assignee are notified, never the person who made the change.

Endpoints involved: POST /bugs, POST /bugs/{id}/assign, POST /bugs/{id}/status, GET /bugs/{id}, GET /projects/{id}/bugs.

Entities touched (business-data-context): entity-bug, state-bug, flow-file-and-triage-bug, flow-notifications.

Features (business-e2e-context): feature-defects (FEAT-022, FEAT-023), journey-file-and-triage-bug.

Journey: invite a teammate and join a workspace

Purpose: grow a team without sharing credentials, while keeping tenants apart. Cross-tenant leakage is the top security risk of a multi-tenant TMS.

  1. An admin or owner issues the invite (workspace:admin; a PAT must be bound to this workspace). The raw token is hashed at rest and returned once inside accept_url (201).
  2. The link travels outside Bunkai (chat, email written by the inviter).
  3. The invitee signs in and posts the token. Order of checks: token exists, workspace live (else 404, indistinguishable from a bad token), not revoked, accepted or expired (409 each), email matches (else 403), not already a member with an equal or higher role (409).
  4. The membership is created or upgraded and the invite stamped accepted (200 with workspace and role).

Endpoints involved: POST /workspaces/{id}/invites, POST /workspaces/{id}/invites/{inviteId}, DELETE /workspaces/{id}/invites/{inviteId}, POST /invites/accept.

Entities touched (business-data-context): entity-invite, state-invite, flow-invite-and-membership, entity-workspace.

Features (business-e2e-context): feature-workspace (FEAT-006), journey-join-workspace-by-invite, cross-feature-active-workspace.

Journey: upgrade a workspace to Cloud

Purpose: revenue. The only flow where money changes hands, and the plan must change only on confirmed payment.

  1. The owner starts a checkout with a seat quantity. The owner check runs before the idempotency row is written, then a billing_checkout_sessions row is opened (one per workspace) before Stripe is called, so a double click cannot open two payments.
  2. The API creates the Stripe Checkout Session with that row id as reference and returns Stripe's hosted URL.
  3. The owner pays on Stripe. Cancelling on Stripe's page returns to the app, which calls the cancel endpoint.
  4. Stripe posts the signed event. Only a paid session upgrades the workspace to cloud and sets purchased seats; an expired or failed async payment releases the lock without a plan change.

Endpoints involved: GET /workspaces/{id}/billing, POST /workspaces/{id}/billing/checkout, POST /workspaces/{id}/billing/checkout/cancel, POST /billing/webhook.

Entities touched (business-data-context): flow-billing-upgrade, state-checkout-session, entity-workspace, integration-stripe.

Features (business-e2e-context): feature-workspace (FEAT-007), journey-upgrade-to-cloud.

Journey: import user stories from Jira

Purpose: start from the requirements a team already has instead of retyping them. The only API flow whose work outlives the request.

  1. A member posts the project and a JQL query (1 to 2,000 characters). A partial unique index allows one queued or running import per project (409 import_in_progress).
  2. The API answers 202 with the job id and starts the worker in the same request's after() slot.
  3. The worker pages Jira search 100 issues at a time with the platform's own Atlassian account, converts each description, extracts criteria, picks or creates a module and upserts the story by Jira key.
  4. The client polls the job until completed (with created, updated and skipped counts and per-issue errors) or failed.

Endpoints involved: POST /imports, GET /imports/{id}.

Entities touched (business-data-context): flow-jira-import, state-async-job, entity-user-story, integration-jira.

Features (business-e2e-context): feature-authoring (FEAT-013), journey-build-project-structure.

Journey: delete and restore a workspace

Purpose: let an owner end a tenant safely. Blast radius is the whole team, and after 30 days it is irreversible.

  1. The owner calls DELETE /workspaces/{id} from a browser (a PAT gets 403; a non-owner 403; an already deleted workspace 404). Other members cannot veto.
  2. In one transaction the workspace is flagged deleted, its bound tokens and pending invites are revoked and a tombstone is written. The API answers 200.
  3. After the response, an after() task emails the restore link to the owner and every active member through Resend; a mail failure does not undo the deletion.
  4. From then on every route answers as if the workspace did not exist, for everyone. Within 30 days the owner can POST /workspaces/{id}/restore (409 if it is not deleted); revoked tokens and invites stay revoked.
  5. After 30 days the daily pg_cron purge deletes the workspace and everything that cascades from it; the tombstone survives.

Endpoints involved: DELETE /workspaces/{id}, POST /workspaces/{id}/restore.

Entities touched (business-data-context): flow-workspace-deletion, state-workspace, integration-resend.

Features (business-e2e-context): feature-workspace (FEAT-009), journey-delete-and-restore-workspace.

Architecture behind the API

One Next.js application on Vercel serves both the UI and /api/v1 as serverless route handlers; there is no separate backend, queue or cache. Business rules live in Postgres functions (bunkai_* RPCs) and Row Level Security; handlers parse, authenticate, call one RPC or an RLS-checked query, and map errors. The system figure is at the top of this map (section overview).

ComponentRolePersistence / integrations touchedWhy it matters for QA
Middleware (middleware.ts)Refreshes the Supabase session cookie on every non-static request; redirects signed-out page visits to /loginSupabase Auth (getUser per request)Never blocks /api/*: an API test without credentials reaches the gateway and gets the envelope 401, not a redirect
Gateway (withApiHandler, lib/api/handler.ts)Request id, JSON access log, posture and scope checks, error envelopenone itselfEvery response carries x-request-id; quote it in bug reports. Any thrown non-API error becomes 500 internal_error
Principal resolution (lib/api/principal.ts, middleware/bearer.ts, user-jwt.ts)Cookie or PAT → one principal with an RLS-scoped clientaccess_tokens (service role), Supabase AuthCookie and PAT reach the same handler code, so one functional test per behaviour plus an auth-matrix test per posture is enough
Route handlers (app/api/v1/**, 104 handlers)Parse with zod (422 on invalid body), call the RPC, shape the responsePostgres via PostgRESTRequest validation is in zod; business validation is in the database (SQLSTATE mapped per domain, error-semantics)
Idempotency (lib/api/idempotency.ts)Replays the first answer for the same Idempotency-Key; 409 on a different body or an in-flight duplicateidempotency_keys (24-hour rows)Required on 4 creates: Tests, Runs, test plan membership, billing checkout; a missing key is 400

Contract (route.openapi.ts per route → public/openapi.json)Generated OpenAPI 102 operations, served at /api/openapi, rendered at /api/docsnoneShapes come from the contract; this map never restates them

Deployment shape: one Vercel project per environment URL; the Vercel cron is registered from production only. Rate limiting: none in the app; only Supabase Auth's own limits surface as 429 on the sign-in family.

Error semantics

Every error from a gateway-wrapped route is one envelope: { error: { code, message, details?, request_id } } with the same id in the x-request-id header. Clients branch on code and, for finer cases, on details.reason; the message is for people. The 4 bypass routes do not use it (the OAuth callback answers { code: "OAUTH_STATE_MISMATCH" } or redirects).

CodeHTTPWhat it means to the caller
bad_request400body is not JSON, a path id is malformed, a required header is missing (Stripe signature), an invalid cursor
idempotency_key_required / idempotency_key_invalid400send an Idempotency-Key of 8 to 128 word characters or dashes on the four idempotent creates
unauthorized401no or bad credential; for PATs always "Invalid token." whatever the cause
forbidden403wrong credential type (cookie-only), missing scope (missing_capability), wrong token binding, or role too low (not_a_member, owner-only actions)
not_found404missing, or in a workspace the caller cannot see (deliberately the same answer); also export not ready or expired
conflict409stale version, closed Run, duplicate active job, idempotency key reuse, invite already used, last owner leaving
slug_collision, checkout_in_progress409retry with a new request / wait for or cancel the open checkout
validation_failed422zod body validation (details = the issues) or a database rule (details.reason names it)
ac_outside_user_story, module_outside_project_subtree, chain_empty, chain_mismatch, chain_invalid, no_executable_steps, environment_invalid, test_outside_plan_project, plan_not_upgradable, seat_quantity_invalid, project_limit_reached, steps_position_invalid422named business rule violations a client can branch on without parsing text
rate_limited429Supabase Auth throttled a sign-in family call
internal_error500anything unmapped, including a database error a mapper does not know (its raw message is passed through)
upstream_error502Supabase Auth or Stripe failed, or the webhook saw an unknown checkout session
payment_processor_unavailable503Stripe unreachable at checkout
method_not_allowed405declared in the envelope; no handler throws it in the snapshot

How database rules become HTTP answers

Business functions raise custom SQLSTATEs in the 45xxx range; each domain has one mapper (lib/atcs/errors.ts, lib/runs/errors.ts, lib/bugs/errors.ts, lib/tests/errors.ts, lib/test-plans/errors.ts, lib/environments/errors.ts, and response helpers for workspaces, modules, stories and notifications). Shared rules: 42501 (RLS or role refusal) → 403 not_a_member; P0002 → 404; unknown codes → 500.

DomainSQLSTATE → answer (selected)
ATC45020 → 422 ac_outside_user_story; 45021 → 422 module_outside_project_subtree; 45022 → 409 version_conflict + current_version; 45024 → 422 tags limit; 23505 → 409 slug_collision
Test45120 → 422 chain_empty; 45122 → 404 (ATC outside workspace); 45123 / 45124 → 422 chain mismatch / invalid; 45125 → 409 version conflict; 45126 → 422 tags
Run45200 → 422 executor mode; 45201 → 422 environment_invalid; 45202 → 422 no_executable_steps; 45204 / 45206 / 45212 → 409 run closed (abort / finish / mark); 45205 → 422 abort reason; 45207 → 422 verdict; 45213 → 422 step status
Bug45300 / 45305 / 45306 / 45307 → 422 provenance outside project or run; 45301 / 45302 / 45303 → 422 title, severity, evidence; 45310 / 45311 → 422 skipped / backward status; 45312 / 45313 → 422 assignee not member / viewer
Test plan45600 to 45602 → 422 lengths; 45603 → 409 plan closed; 45604 → 422 test_outside_plan_project; 45605 → 422 nothing selected; 45606 → 404 Test not in plan
Workspacedelete or restore by a non-owner → 403; deleted or missing → 404; restore of a live workspace → 409; leave as only workspace or last owner → 409

Anti-enumeration: sign-in, magic link and token checks never reveal whether an account or token exists; POST /auth/check-email does, on purpose (see discovery-gaps).

Coherence check

  • Every journey touches entities present in the data map; no orphan entity was found.
  • Every journey maps to an e2e journey and feature. API-only paths without a UI feature: the headless sign-up, confirm and sign-in PAT minting (covered by journey-automate-via-api), the digest cron, the Stripe webhook, GET /me.
  • Integrations listed by the e2e map that reach the API boundary (Supabase, Stripe, Resend, Jira, GitHub and Google OAuth, Vercel) all appear in integrations, and nothing extra.

Discovery gaps

  • No live API call was made (brief: read-only). Every status code, message and ordering here is read from code at origin/staging 98ee1b4; behaviour on the running staging deployment was not observed.
  • The QA repo's synced types are not usable: api/openapi-types.ts declares paths = any and api/schemas/ holds only auth and example types (last touched 2026-09-30). bun run api:sync was not run (out of scope).
  • Workspace-bound tokens: the binding is enforced only by the 7 workspace:admin handlers (assertWorkspaceContext). Project- and resource-scoped routes rely on the owner's RLS only, so a token bound to workspace A appears able to act in workspace B where its owner is a member. Not verified live; whether that is intended is a product question.
  • POST /auth/check-email has no app-level rate limiter: its own comment says Supabase throttling does not cover it and the limiter is a documented follow-up (ADR-0007). This contradicts the data map's "mitigated by rate limiting".
  • The invite issue handler still writes the full accept URL, raw token included, to stdout (app/api/v1/workspaces/[id]/invites/route.ts), so log readers can redeem a pending invite (same finding as the infra map NFR-SEC-010).
  • Headless sign-in and confirm mint a global, never-expiring PAT with atc:read, atc:write, run:execute unless the caller asks otherwise; with about 8,900 non-revoked tokens in the shared database (data map), test runs likely accumulate live credentials. How the QA repo's own bun run api:login sets expiry was not checked.
  • Unmapped database errors return 500 with the raw database message in error.message; how much schema detail that leaks in practice was not measured.
  • Bug writes need atc:write and reports need atc:read: there is no bug or report scope. Intended scope design or a gap: not confirmed.
  • POST /invites/accept writes the membership and then stamps the invite in two separate service-role writes; a failure between them was not analysed.
  • Contradictions with the infra map (built at e88512e): it says only GET /workspaces and GET /me accept a PAT, scopes are not enforced, idempotency is unused, and sign-up mints a PAT; current code has 74 scope-gated handlers, 4 idempotent creates, and sign-up returns 202 with the PAT issued at /auth/confirm.
  • Contradiction with the data map: flow-compose-test-and-plan says POST /tests has the idempotency key "supported"; the handler requires it (400 idempotency_key_required).
  • Contradiction with the domain map (e88512e): it expands ATC as "Atomic Test Component"; code says "Acceptance Test Case".
  • Stripe webhook endpoint registration, Stripe test mode, OAuth provider setup and Resend delivery per environment live in external dashboards and were not verified.
  • On staging the digest cron is not registered; a manual call needs CRON_SECRET, whose presence on staging was not checked.
  • Journey cap: 7 journeys traced. Data export, environments, test plans, reports and notifications are documented as groups only, not as traced journeys.
